title: Binary search when looking up a character in a dictionary
summary: In a dictionary ordered alphabetically by pinyin, look up any character whose pinyin starts with r. Across 5 frames, Step 1 sets the initial search range and Steps 2 through 5 each open to the midpoint once.
description: Each frame arranges all 26 letter blocks from a to z left to right. Green marks letters still within the active search range, cyan highlights target letter r, and light gray marks discarded letters; in Steps 2 through 5, an upward pointer labeled “Midpoint” underneath marks the letter opened on that step.

frames.title: State the lookup goal and initial range
frames.explanation: The initial search range covers all 26 letters from a to z before opening to any page. Target r is cyan, and the other 25 letters are green.
frames.key_state: Initial state: the search range covers all letters from a to z, with the goal of finding a character whose pinyin starts with r.
frames.announcement: State the lookup goal—finding a character whose pinyin starts with r—across the full alphabetically ordered initial range of all 26 letters from a to z.

frames.title: Open to midpoint letter m and discard the first half
frames.explanation: First open the dictionary near its midpoint, where the pointer lands on m. Since r comes after m, discard a through m so they turn light gray; the remaining letters n through z stay colored, with target r in cyan.
frames.key_state: Opening at the midpoint lands on m; since r comes after m, discard a through m, leaving range n through z.
frames.announcement: Open the dictionary near its midpoint to find initial letter m; since r comes after m, discard the first half a through m and narrow the search range to n through z.

frames.title: Open to midpoint letter t of the remaining section and discard the second half
frames.explanation: Open the remaining range n through z at its midpoint, where the pointer lands on t. Since r comes before t, discard t through z. Now both a through m on the left and t through z on the right are light gray, leaving only n through s colored, with r in cyan.
frames.key_state: Opening at the midpoint of remaining range n through z lands on t; since r comes before t, discard t through z. The active range is now n through s, with a through m on the left and t through z on the right discarded.
frames.announcement: Open the remaining section at its midpoint to find initial letter t; since r comes before t, discard the second half t through z and narrow the search range to n through s.

frames.title: Open to midpoint letter p of the remaining section and discard the first half again
frames.explanation: Open the remaining range n through s at its midpoint, where the pointer lands on p. Since r comes after p, discard n through p. Now a through p on the left and t through z on the right are light gray, leaving only q, r, and s colored: q and s in green, and r in cyan.
frames.key_state: Opening at the midpoint of remaining range n through s lands on p; since r comes after p, discard n through p. Only q, r, and s remain active, with a through p on the left and t through z on the right discarded.
frames.announcement: Open the remaining section at its midpoint to find initial letter p; since r comes after p, discard the first half n through p, leaving only q, r, and s in the search range.

frames.title: Open to midpoint letter r and complete the lookup
frames.explanation: Open the remaining range q, r, and s at its midpoint, where the pointer lands directly on target r—finding a character whose pinyin starts with r and completing the task. This is Step 5, and the 4th midpoint check. The diagram keeps q and s in green and r in cyan to show the range just before this check, while a through p and t through z remain light gray.
frames.key_state: Lookup complete: opening at the midpoint of remaining range q, r, and s lands on target letter r.
frames.announcement: Open at the midpoint of remaining range q, r, and s to hit target initial letter r directly, completing the dictionary lookup.
